summary: The starter prompt gives a clear, actionable goal (Node.js + LlamaIndex agent, DiskANN, 20k ingest script, UI, config-file handling, and commented code). Several implementation details are left to the builder (driver version, embedding model, index tuning, session-store choice, README/test details), but installed DocumentDB skills and the provided run-environment notes cover much of the missing infrastructure and best-practice guidance. No blocking unknowns — the build can start but will require the builder to pick defaults for a handful of technical choices.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LlamaIndex agent that reads co-purchase order history from Azure DocumentDB, generates product embeddings, stores them in a DiskANN index, and uses agent memory to personalise recommendations per session."
rubric.note: The business problem (product recommendations from co-purchase history) and what to demonstrate are explicit.
Single-agent using the LlamaIndex agent framework is explicit.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Node.js 24 (the run-environment notes say Node.js 24 is available).
rubric.note: Prompt states Node.js; run-environment skill_md supplies Node.js 24.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official mongodb npm driver (package 'mongodb') pinned to a recent stable major compatible with Node 24 (e.g. ^5.0), and follow the documentdb-driver guidance to instantiate a singleton MongoClient.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't name which MongoDB Node driver or version to use; the documentdb-driver skill provides best-practice patterns but not a concrete version choice.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the provided live, vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) and the database named 'sample_retail_02'.
rubric.note: Run-environment notes explicitly describe the available cluster and DB to use.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Use a config file for the Azure DocumentDB connection string and display a clear error if the connection string is missing or invalid."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Read connection string from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime; include a .env.example with a placeholder; never write the real secret to repo or logs.
rubric.note: Prompt requires config-file usage and clear error; run-environment adds the DOCUMENTDB_URI convention and .env.example guidance.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "reads co-purchase order history from Azure DocumentDB"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create an 'orders' collection in database 'sample_retail_02' with docs like { orderId, userId, products: [productId], timestamp } and a 'products' collection for metadata; use no sharding for the sample.
rubric.note: The prompt says to read co-purchase history but does not define collection names or document schema. The data-modeling skill gives patterns but not exact shapes — the builder will pick a simple 'orders' document shape.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "include a script to ingest 20,000 product purchase transactions"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: The ingest script will synthesize 20,000 sample order documents (no external dataset), inserting them into the 'orders' collection. The data will be synthetic and licensed as generated by the project.
rubric.note: Prompt requires a 20k ingest script but doesn't require external dataset or licensing details; builders typically generate synthetic data.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a DiskANN vector index with dimensionality matching the chosen embedding model (e.g., 1536), using sensible defaults for DiskANN build/search params (leave lBuild/lSearch default or documented values recommended by documentdb-vector-search). Also create simple single-field indexes for lookup queries (e.g., productId).
rubric.note: DiskANN is required, but concrete index parameters (dimension, L* tuning) are not provided; vector-search and indexing skills provide guidance the builder will follow.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a hosted embedding provider such as OpenAI (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) with credentials from OPENAI_API_KEY; use LlamaIndex Node bindings to call embeddings and an LLM (e.g., OpenAI gpt-4o-family or gpt-4o-mini) for reasoning. Document the chosen models in README.
rubric.note: Prompt names LlamaIndex and asks for embeddings but does not pick an embedding model or specify where model credentials come from; no installed skill covers LLM/embedding provider selection.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "The agent should accept a product ID and return the top 5 recommended items with reasoning." "artistic UI to look like an online retailer's website."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a simple web UI (React or plain HTML/JS served by Express) with an input for product ID and a results panel showing five recommendations plus textual reasoning; also expose a /recommend API endpoint accepting productId and returning JSON.
rubric.note: Prompt requires both an artistic retailer-style UI and an input/return contract; UI framework is left to the implementer.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned" (skill_md).
rubric.note: Prompt/run-environment explicitly uses an existing cluster; provisioning new infrastructure is not required for the sample.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add README commands: npm install, npm run seed (to ingest 20k), npm start, and instructions to set DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY; basic manual verification steps will be included but no exhaustive automated tests.
rubric.note: Starter prompt asks for the app but does not specify exact run/test commands or test coverage expectations.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "accept a product ID and return the top 5 recommended items with reasoning"; "ingest 20,000 product purchase transactions"; "artistic UI"; "config file"; "detailed comments before each method"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Treat the prompt's bullet items as acceptance criteria: app runs locally, seed inserts 20k, vector index built and persisted, /recommend returns five items with reasoning, and the UI demonstrates recommended items.
rubric.note: The prompt lists deliverables that can serve as done criteria but does not define pass/fail conditions or verification details.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: No cloud provisioning will be done; keep cost low (no high-throughput tiers), data will be synthetic, and the sample is educational (not production-ready security/hardening).
rubric.note: No cost, licensing, or compliance constraints are specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Use a config file for the Azure DocumentDB connection string"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a standard Node repo layout (package.json, src/, public/, README.md), include .env.example, package-lock.json or pinned versions in package.json, and add npm scripts for seed/start/test. Follow minimal telemetry/attribution (none required).
rubric.note: Prompt asks for a config file; broader repo conventions are not specified.

contradictions: The prompt says "Using the Azure DocumentDB skill" but there is no installed skill named exactly "Azure DocumentDB skill". There are many documentdb-* skills available (e.g., documentdb-driver, documentdb-vector-search) and a run-environment skill_md, but the exact skill name referenced in the prompt is not present.
questions_for_author: Which embedding model and provider should the sample use (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small 1536-dim, a local HuggingFace model, or something else)? This determines index dimensionality and config.
Which LLM/provider should be used for the LlamaIndex 'reasoning' output (and should model creds be expected in env vars like OPENAI_API_KEY)?
Which MongoDB Node.js driver and minimum version should the sample target (e.g., 'mongodb' npm package ^5.0)?
How should per-session agent memory be persisted for personalization: in-memory per server process, browser session storage, or a server-side session store (Redis / DB)?
Do you require an explicit .env.example and README with exact run/test commands, or should the builder create a minimal README and .env.example with placeholders?
requirements_at_risk: Use the Azure DocumentDB skill to read co-purchase order history from Azure DocumentDB (the prompt instructs 'Using the Azure DocumentDB skill' but no single installed skill matches that exact name; the builder may not produce an adapter explicitly called that).
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output (embedding model not specified in prompt; builder must choose — risk that chosen model and index dimensions are inconsistent).

The vector index parameters are chosen for the catalog size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one (index tuning parameters are not provided and README instructions are not requested explicitly).

A seed script loads sample products and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data (prompt requires a 20k ingest script but does not require idempotency or seeding of product metadata and index creation semantics).
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails (error-handling behavior for search/embedding failures is not specified).
Search results include the similarity score (prompt requires top 5 items with reasoning but does not require exposing numeric similarity scores).
Dependencies are pinned in a lock or requirements file (prompt doesn't mention pinning; Node projects may rely on package-lock.json but requirement asked for pinned dependencies explicitly).
Unit tests run without a live cluster (prompt doesn't mention tests or test strategy to run offline/mocked).
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type (the run environment provides an existing cluster; the prompt doesn't request IaC).
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up (prompt asks for the app but didn't explicitly ask for a README with full instructions).
